artifacts.notes: One header line and 121 data lines, one physical line per sense line, with no embedded tabs or newlines. Columns: seq, element_key, printed_title, line, line_class, text, source_url. Thirteen element keys: kyrie, gloria-in-excelsis, nicene-creed, apostles-creed, sursum-corda, sanctus-benedictus, agnus-dei, agnus-dei-alternative, lords-prayer, and gloria-patri-layout-1 through -3. THIS IS NOT THE ROMAN MISSAL'S ENGLISH and must never be served as though it were. It is the ecumenical text; the Roman Missal's is the International Commission on English in the Liturgy's, and the two differ where a reader will notice at once - here the Sursum corda answers "And also with you" and the Nicene Creed opens "We believe in one God", against "And with your spirit" and "I believe in one God" in the 2011 Roman Missal. Three things the site's own pages do that are reproduced as found rather than corrected: the Sanctus page sets a stray bare paragraph "Hosanna in the highest." above its list, which is not part of the list and is therefore not carried; the Gloria Patri is given in three alternative line layouts of one text, all three carried; and Layout 3 of the Gloria Patri prints "and to the Son,." with both a comma and a stop, which stands as the page sets it. The Agnus Dei is given in two forms, the Consultation's own and a more traditional alternative, and both are carried because the choice between them is the reader's and not this project's. Not a liturgical book: nothing here is approved for use in the Roman Rite by the fact of being recorded.
artifacts.rights_basis: The rightsholder grants free use in terms, on its own permissions page and again in its Guidelines for Reproducing ELLC Texts: "The texts in Praying Together may be used freely and without the need for prior permission. The liturgical text(s) should be properly acknowledged." Both statements were read from bytes fetched and hashed by this project on 2026-07-31 and are registered as the sibling permissions-page and reproduction-guidelines artifacts. The grant is to the liturgical texts only; the Consultation's introduction and its notes on each text are expressly excluded and nothing here reproduces them. The acknowledgement the grant requires is: English translations of the Kyrie eleison, Gloria in excelsis, the Nicene Creed, the Apostles' Creed, the Sursum corda, the Sanctus and Benedictus, the Agnus Dei, the Lord's Prayer and the Gloria Patri, (c) 1998, English Language Liturgical Consultation (ELLC), and used by permission. www.englishtexts.org. That wording must travel with the text to every place it is served; it is carried in the ordo-missae inventory that consumes this artifact and rendered by the browser at the point of use.

artifacts.notes: The page states the grant in terms: "The texts in Praying Together may be used freely and without the need for prior permission. The liturgical text(s) should be properly acknowledged." It gives the acknowledgement wording that must be used - "English translations of (text), (c) 1998, English Language Liturgical Consultation (ELLC), and used by permission. www.englishtexts.org" - and asks, without requiring it, that the Secretary be informed of uses in service and prayer books. It is a mutable web page: this record fixes the state read on 2026-07-31 and asserts nothing about any later state.
artifacts.rights_basis: The exact bytes are the Consultation's own website page, with its markup, navigation and site design. No distribution grant covers that markup, so the bytes are recorded and not retained. This artifact is registered as the evidence for a rights position, not as a text to reuse; the grant it evidences is quoted in the rights_basis of the sibling common-texts-en artifact.

artifacts.notes: This is the document that bounds the grant, and the bound matters here. It repeats the permission for the liturgical texts and then states the exception: "The reproduction of other texts from Praying Together such as the Introduction or notes on each text, does require permission from the Secretary." Each text's page on the Consultation's site carries such notes below the text; none of them is reproduced by this project. It also states two expectations about presentation - that the printed sense lines be kept, and that a modified or adapted text carry "(adapted)" in its acknowledgement - and gives the parallel acknowledgement for the older ICET texts.
artifacts.rights_basis: The Consultation's own guidance document, dated July 2017. Its final section permits free reproduction of ELLC material other than the liturgical texts for non-commercial use, which would very likely cover retaining this file; the question was not settled, and it does not need to be, because nothing here reuses the document's wording beyond the grant it states. The bytes are recorded and not retained.

edition.notes: The 1998 revision supersedes the International Consultation on English Texts' Prayers we have in common (1970, 1971, 1975), whose texts remain in use in some churches and which the Consultation's reproduction guidelines cover under a parallel acknowledgement. The Consultation prepares the texts in standard American spelling and expects other standards to be substituted where preferred, and it expects the printed sense lines to be kept; both expectations are recorded here rather than acted on, and the texts are carried exactly as the site sets them. This edition is dated by the copyright year the Consultation's own acknowledgement wording requires; the site state actually read is fixed by the exact hashes on this edition's artifacts.
edition.publication: English Language Liturgical Consultation, 1998. The texts and the Consultation's commentary on each are published on the Consultation's own site at https://www.englishtexts.org/, one page per text.
edition.title: Praying Together, the 1998 revision of the ELLC common liturgical texts

work.author: English Language Liturgical Consultation (ELLC), successor to the International Consultation on English Texts (ICET)
work.description: The ecumenical English translations of the liturgical texts the Western churches hold in common: the Lord's Prayer, Kyrie eleison, Gloria in excelsis, the Nicene and Apostles' Creeds, the Sursum corda, the Sanctus and Benedictus, the Agnus Dei, the Gloria Patri, the Te Deum, and the three gospel canticles. ELLC is an ecumenical consultation of English-speaking liturgical bodies and is not an organ of any one church. These translations are therefore NOT the approved liturgical English of the Roman Rite: the Roman Missal's English is the International Commission on English in the Liturgy's, a different body with a different text, and the two must never be conflated. Where the two are compared the difference is visible at once - this work reads 'And also with you' where the 2011 Roman Missal reads 'And with your spirit', and 'We believe in one God' where it reads 'I believe in one God'.
work.title: Praying Together
